chapter: New Orleans dance scene of the 1920s
title: Santo Pecora and Joe Focco's show band at the Palace
summary: Pecora soloing at 16 or 17 with Focco's band, which was a show band rather than a jazz band.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: There's one thing that I can remember very clearly. I can see him just like it was yesterday. And that was Santo Pecora. You know, he must have learned his instrument at a very early age, because I don't think he was more than 16 or 17 years old when he was playing with Joe Focco's band at the Old Palace. And he was taking solos and bringing down the house at that time. And I can recall very clearly.
Would Joe Focco let him play jazz at the Palace? Oh, yes. I always thought of him as a legit man. Well, he was.

As a matter of fact, my father gave me his first job in this town. But when you say jazz, it was not exactly a jazz band. It was, you might say, a show band. And they injected a little jazz into the... But it was certainly not a jazz band, no.
Joe Focco wasn't from New Orleans, or...?
I think, if I recall correctly, he was not born here. He came over from the old country. I think I'm correct in saying that.
